fanoutqa_011307.x:
Geography of the Philippines :: Physical geography :: Geology :: chunk_0003
The [Philippine Archipelago](/wiki/Philippine_Archipelago "Philippine Archipelago") is geologically part of the [Philippine Mobile Belt](/wiki/Philippine_Mobile_Belt "Philippine Mobile Belt") located between the [Philippine Sea Plate](/wiki/Philippine_Sea_Plate "Philippine Sea Plate"), the South China Sea Basin of the [Eurasian Plate](/wiki/Eurasian_Plate "Eurasian Plate"), and the [Sunda Plate](/wiki/Sunda_Plate "Sunda Plate"). The [Philippine Trench](/wiki/Philippine_Trench "Philippine Trench") (also called the Mindanao Trench) is a [submarine trench](/wiki/Submarine_trench "Submarine trench") 1,320 kilometers (820 mi) in length found directly east of the Philippine Mobile Belt and is the result of a collision of tectonic plates. The Philippine Sea Plate is [subducting](/wiki/Subducting "Subducting") under the Philippine Mobile Belt at the rate of about 16 centimeters (6.3 in) per year. The [Philippine Fault System](/wiki/Philippine_Fault_System "Philippine Fault System") consists of a series of seismic [faults](/wiki/Fault_(geology) "Fault (geology)") that produce several [earthquakes](/wiki/Earthquake "Earthquake") per year, most of which are not felt. The Galathea Depth in the [Philippine Trench](/wiki/Philippine_Trench "Philippine Trench") is the deepest point in the country and the [third deepest in the world](/wiki/List_of_submarine_topographical_features#List_of_oceanic_trenches "List of submarine topographical features"). The trench is located in the Philippine Sea.[[32]](#cite_note-32)

The islands are composed of volcanic, coral, principal rock formations. Twelve main forest formations are classified, which are the [Mangrove](/wiki/Mangrove "Mangrove") forest, Beach forest, Freshwater swamp forest, [Peat swamp](/wiki/Peat_swamp_forest "Peat swamp forest") forest, [Molave](/wiki/Vitex_parviflora "Vitex parviflora") forest (Forest over [Limestone](/wiki/Limestone "Limestone")), Bon

With a coastline of approximately 500 km (311 mi), it is situated at the head of the [Persian Gulf](/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf") in the northeastern edge of the [Arabian Peninsula](/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula "Arabian Peninsula"), bordering [Iraq](/wiki/Iraq "Iraq") to [the north](/wiki/Iraq%E2%80%93Kuwait_border "Iraq–Kuwait border") and [Saudi Arabia](/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia") to [the south](/wiki/Kuwait%E2%80%93Saudi_Arabia_border "Kuwait–Saudi Arabia border").[[16]](#cite_note-cia-18) Kuwait is geographically the closest Gulf country to [mainland Iran](/wiki/Iranian_plateau "Iranian plateau") (separated only by a small [Iraqi coastline](/wiki/Al-Faw_peninsula "Al-Faw peninsula")).[[17]](#cite_note-19) The country is a small [city-state](/wiki/City-state "City-state");[[18]](#cite_note-20) most of the population reside in the [urban agglomeration](/wiki/Urban_area "Urban area") of [Kuwait City](/wiki/Kuwait_City "Kuwait City"), the capital and largest city.[[19]](#cite_note-21) As of 2024, Kuwait has a population of 4.82 million, of which 1.53 million are [Kuwaiti citizens](/wiki/Kuwaiti_nationality_law "Kuwaiti nationality law") while the remaining 3.29 million are [foreign nationals](/wiki/Expatriates_in_Kuwait "Expatriates in Kuwait") from over 100 countries.[[20]](#cite_note-:1-22) In 2024, Kuwait had the world's seventh [largest number of foreign nationals as a percentage of the population](/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_by_immigrant_and_emigrant_population "List of sovereign states by immigrant and emigrant population"), where its citizens make up fewer than 30% of the overall population.[[21]](#cite_note-23)

Crocus :: Description :: General :: chunk_0001
*Crocus* display the general characteristics of family [Iridaceae](/wiki/Iridaceae "Iridaceae"), which include basal cauline (arising from the aerial stem) leaves that sheath the stem base, [hermaphrodite](/wiki/Hermaphrodite "Hermaphrodite") flowers that are relatively large and showy, the perianth petaloid with two whorls of three tepals each and septal nectaries. The flowers have three stamens and a gynoecium of three united carpels and an inferior ovary, three locules and axile placentation with fruit that is a loculicidal capsule.[[2]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoldblatt_et_al1998295–296-2)

*Crocus* is an [acaulescent](/wiki/Acaulescent "Acaulescent") (lacking a visible lower stem above ground) diminutive seasonal cormous (growing from [corms](/wiki/Corm "Corm")) [herbaceous perennial](/wiki/Perennial_plant "Perennial plant") [geophytic](/wiki/Geophytic "Geophytic") genus.[[3]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMeerow201223-3) The corms are symmetrical and [globose](/wiki/Globose "Globose") or [oblate](/wiki/Glossary_of_botanical_terms#oblate "Glossary of botanical terms") (round in shape with flatted tops and bottoms), and are covered with tunic leaves that are fibrous, membranous or [coriaceous](/wiki/Coriaceous "Coriaceous") (leathery). The corms produce fibrous [roots](/wiki/Root "Root"), and contractile roots which adjust the corms depth in the soil, which may be pulled as deep as 20 centimetres (8 in) into the soil.[[4]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoldblatt_et_al1998-4)[[5]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZhao_et_al2004-5) The roots appear randomly from the lower part of the corm, but in a few species, from a basal ridge.[[6]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoldblatt_et_al1998297-6)

fanoutqa_021291.t: Yellow River :: Geography :: Lower reaches :: chunk_0015
fanoutqa_021291.x:
Yellow River :: Geography :: Lower reaches :: chunk_0015
Main article: [Yellow River delta](/wiki/Yellow_River_delta "Yellow River delta")

In the lower reaches, from [Zhengzhou](/wiki/Zhengzhou "Zhengzhou") to its mouth, a distance of 786 km (488 mi), the river is confined to a [levee](/wiki/Levee "Levee")-lined course as it flows to the northeast across the [North China Plain](/wiki/North_China_Plain "North China Plain") before emptying into the [Bohai Sea](/wiki/Bohai_Sea "Bohai Sea"). The basin area in this stage is only 23,000 square kilometers (8,900 sq mi), a mere 3% of the total, because few tributaries add to the flow in this stage; nearly all rivers to the south drain into the [Huai River](/wiki/Huai_River "Huai River"), whereas those to the north drain into the [Hai River](/wiki/Hai_River "Hai River"). The Huai River Basin, for example, is separated from the Yellow River Basin by the south dike of the Yellow River.[[67]](#cite_note-70) The total drop in elevation of the lower reaches is 93.6 m (307 ft), with an average grade of 0.012%.

The silts received from the middle reaches form sediments here, elevating the river bed. Excessive sediment deposits have raised the riverbed several meters above the surrounding ground. That is why this part of the river is called [the 'Earth Suspended River'](/wiki/The_Earth_Suspended_River "The Earth Suspended River"). At [Kaifeng](/wiki/Kaifeng "Kaifeng"), Henan, the Yellow River is 10 meters (33 ft) above the ground level.[[68]](#cite_note-71)

The [UEFA Champions League](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"), known until 1992 as the European Champion Clubs' Cup or colloquially as the European Cup, is an annual [association football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") cup competition organised by [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") since 1955. Originally a straight knockout competition open only to champion clubs, the tournament was expanded during the 1990s to incorporate a round-robin group phase and more teams. The expansion resulted in more games being played, increasing players' goalscoring chances; thus the rankings are weighted in favour of modern players: only six out of the 50 players on the list never competed in the reformed Champions League.

With 140 goals, [Cristiano Ronaldo](/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") is currently the all-time top scorer in the Champions League, with [Lionel Messi](/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") and [Robert Lewandowski](/wiki/Robert_Lewandowski "Robert Lewandowski") being the only other players to have reached triple figures. Ronaldo has also finished as the top scorer [for the most individual seasons](#By_player) in the competition's history, doing so seven times.

Main article: [History of Monaco](/wiki/History_of_Monaco "History of Monaco")

Monaco was first mentioned by the Greek historian [Hecataeus of Miletus](/wiki/Hecataeus_of_Miletus "Hecataeus of Miletus"), who referred to it as "*Monoikos*, a [Ligurian](/wiki/Ligures "Ligures") town".[[24]](#cite_note-reinach-27)[[25]](#cite_note-28) [Strabo](/wiki/Strabo "Strabo") referred to it as *Monoikon [limen](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%CE%BB%CE%B9%CE%BC%CE%AE%CE%BD "wikt:λιμήν")*, explaining that *Monoikos* (Greek for "the solitary one") was another name for [Heracles](/wiki/Heracles "Heracles"), who had a temple here;[[26]](#cite_note-29) it is possible, however, that it is an alteration of an older Ligurian name.[[24]](#cite_note-reinach-27)

In 1191, the [Holy Roman Empire](/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire") granted Monaco to the [Genoese](/wiki/Republic_of_Genoa "Republic of Genoa") in return for cracking down on pirates. By the early 1200s, the Genoese had built a castle on the rock and were utilizing the port. An ousted branch of a Genoese family, the [Grimaldis](/wiki/House_of_Grimaldi "House of Grimaldi"), captured it in 1297 by posing as monks, but then had to contest it for a century before gaining official control. Though the [Republic of Genoa](/wiki/Republic_of_Genoa "Republic of Genoa") would last until the 19th century, it allowed the Grimaldi family to keep Monaco. Likewise, both France and Spain left it alone for hundreds of years due to agreements with either of them, especially for defense. France annexed it in the [French Revolution](/wiki/French_Revolution "French Revolution") at the end of the 18th century, but after the defeat of Napoleon it was put under the care of the [Kingdom of Sardinia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Sardinia_(1720%E2%80%931861) "Kingdom of Sardinia (1720–1861)").

After playing for St. Paul in the 1997 season, Drew was selected in the first round of the [1998 MLB draft](/wiki/1998_Major_League_Baseball_draft "1998 Major League Baseball draft"), fifth overall, by the [St. Louis Cardinals](/wiki/St._Louis_Cardinals "St. Louis Cardinals"). In June he signed a $7 million contract,[[5]](#cite_note-rs1998-5) then hit .316 through 26 games with the [Triple-A](/wiki/Triple-A_(baseball) "Triple-A (baseball)") [Memphis Redbirds](/wiki/Memphis_Redbirds "Memphis Redbirds"). He was recalled by the Cardinals and made his debut on September 8, 1998—the game in which teammate [Mark McGwire](/wiki/Mark_McGwire "Mark McGwire") broke the [single-season home run record](/wiki/1998_Major_League_Baseball_home_run_record_chase "1998 Major League Baseball home run record chase") previously held by [Roger Maris](/wiki/Roger_Maris "Roger Maris"). Drew's first [at bat](/wiki/At_bat "At bat"), in the sixth inning, resulted in a [strikeout](/wiki/Strikeout "Strikeout"), and he finished the night 0-for-2. He ended up going 15-for-36 (.417) during 1998, with five home runs.

On August 9, on what would have been Drew's first game in Philadelphia, he sat out, citing a bruised right hand. In an attempt to confuse the Philadelphia fans, he did not wear his own jersey that night, which instead was worn by bullpen catcher, Jeff Murphy. The attempt failed, however, and he was booed and heckled throughout [batting practice](/wiki/Batting_practice "Batting practice"). The only time he received cheers was when he booted three consecutive grounders in the outfield while his teammates were taking batting practice.[[7]](#cite_note-7) On August 10, 1999, in Drew's first game at [Veterans Stadium](/wiki/Veterans_Stadium "Veterans Stadium") in Philadelphia, he was booed loudly, and even had batteries thrown at him by two fans. fanoutqa_012843.t: Robert Burns Woodward :: Research and career :: Organic syntheses and Nobel Prize :: part 02 :: chunk_0005
fanoutqa_012843.x:
Robert Burns Woodward :: Research and career :: Organic syntheses and Nobel Prize :: part 02 :: chunk_0005
In the early 1950s, Woodward, along with the British chemist [Geoffrey Wilkinson](/wiki/Geoffrey_Wilkinson "Geoffrey Wilkinson"), then at Harvard, postulated a novel structure for [ferrocene](/wiki/Ferrocene "Ferrocene"), a compound consisting of a combination of an organic molecule with iron.[[9]](#cite_note-9) This marked the beginning of the field of [transition metal](/wiki/Transition_metal "Transition metal") [organometallic chemistry](/wiki/Organometallic_chemistry "Organometallic chemistry") which grew into an industrially very significant field.[[10]](#cite_note-10) Wilkinson won the Nobel Prize for this work in 1973, along with [Ernst Otto Fischer](/wiki/Ernst_Otto_Fischer "Ernst Otto Fischer").[[11]](#cite_note-11) Some historians think that Woodward should have shared this prize along with Wilkinson. Remarkably, Woodward himself thought so, and voiced his thoughts in a letter sent to the Nobel Committee.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

Woodward won the Nobel Prize in 1965 for his synthesis of complex organic molecules. He had been nominated a total of 111 times from 1946 to 1965.[[13]](#cite_note-13) In his Nobel lecture, he described the total synthesis of the antibiotic cephalosporin, and claimed that he had pushed the synthesis schedule so that it would be completed around the time of the Nobel ceremony.

Three powertrain options are available, although unlike the ID.4, the ID.5 comes with just one battery capacity, which is 77 kWh.
